finding_quote: [blocking] Dialog trap does not skip hidden content. `getFocusable` checks only the element's own computed `display`, not its ancestors, and ignores `visibility`.
_prompt:
You are matching code-review findings against a known bug. Reply with ONLY a JSON object.

KNOWN BUG: The dialog's focus trap counts hidden or tabIndex=-1 elements as tabbable (for example the library's own hidden TabPanels inside a Dialog), so Tab moves focus somewhere invisible.

Rules:
- Answer "yes" only if the text describes THIS specific bug: the same faulty behaviour in the same situation. A finding about a nearby but different behaviour (another header, another edge case, a different race) is "no".
- A finding that says the behaviour was checked and PASSED, or that the code handles it correctly, is "no".
- Wording does not matter; the behaviour does.

=== REVIEW FINDINGS ===
- [blocking] Dialog focus return fails with autoFocus. Click the trigger, then the child `<input autoFocus>` takes focus during commit, before the layout effect records `previous`. So `previous` is the input, which unmounts, and focus lands on body. Repro: `D8b` in the probe, `expect(trig).toHaveFocus()` → received `<body>`. The same flow without autoFocus passes (`D8`, `D8c`). Fix: capture `document.activeElement` before the open commit, e.g. in the trigger's handler or a ref updated on open.
- [blocking] Dialog trap does not skip hidden content. `getFocusable` checks only the element's own computed `display`, not its ancestors, and ignores `visibility`. Repro: `D10`, with `<div style={{display:"none"}}><button>` and `<button style={{visibility:"hidden"}}>` in the dialog. Tab order came out `displaynone, visHidden, last, first` instead of `last, first, last, first`. In a browser, `focus()` on these is a no-op, so focus gets stuck instead of wrapping. The README only promises `hidden`-attribute skipping, so either the code or the README needs to change to match the criterion "hidden elements are skipped".
- [minor] README Combobox says it "accepts any input props except ... `role`", but `type="text"` is set after the spread and silently overrides any passed `type`. Not reproduced as a failure; only read from the code.
- [minor] Dialog backdrop closes on `click` alone, not on mousedown+click as the criterion words it. Not reproduced: a drag from inside to the backdrop produces no backdrop click, since the two elements are siblings.
